title: Monotonicity in a Hill spectral band
statement: For a real smooth periodic one-dimensional Schrödinger operator, is the Floquet phase strictly monotone inside a band when the Bloch branch is fixed by a positive-current orientation?
status: As of November 2026, yes. With \(j=\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\psi_x)>0\), differentiation gives \(p^{\prime}(E)=(2j)^{-1}\int_{x_0}^{x_0+T}|\psi|^2dx>0\). The reciprocal branch has opposite orientation. This is classical Floquet theory; compare \citet[Ch.~II, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}.

title: Supplementary data for the periodic inverse spectral problem
statement: What information, in addition to periodic spectral band data, determines a periodic Schrödinger potential?
status: As of November 2026, in the smooth real nonsingular finite-gap class discussed here, a suitable degree-g divisor, including the sheet choice in each closed gap interval and a fixed base point, supplies the missing phase data and parametrizes the isospectral torus. \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity} and \citet[Ch.~II, \S3]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} verify this answer. The present occurrences do not supply a theorem for arbitrary periodic potentials with infinitely many open gaps.

title: Continuous functions on the product-sequence ray space
statement: For \(S=(\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb R_{>0}\) with the quotient of the product topology, is every continuous real function constant?
status: As of November 2026, yes; the exact example was published in 1967 by \citet[introduction]{gelfandfuchs1967topology}. The earlier occurrence had no separate exact problem identifier. This is a settled explanatory example, not a new open problem.

title: Discontinuous minimizers of elliptic vectorial variational integrals
statement: Do uniformly elliptic vectorial variational problems with smooth or analytic coefficient dependence admit a discontinuous energy-class minimizer?
status: As of November 2026, yes, in the broad class with dependence on the unknown itself; the Giusti--Miranda example dates from 1968, as verified through \citet[\S3.2]{mingione2006regularity}. This does not assert that the repaired homogeneous PDE in the audit is its Euler--Lagrange equation or that every dimension supports the same minimizing example.

title: Finite-gap spectra and stationary KdV characterization
statement: For real smooth periodic potentials, characterize when the whole-line Schr\"odinger spectrum has only finitely many open bounded gaps, and relate this to stationary equations of the KdV hierarchy.
status: As of November 2026, solved: stationary implies finite-gap in \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic}, published July 1974; the converse appears in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974 and published later that year. See also \citet[Chapter 2, \S2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. This is distinct from the supplementary-data inverse problem GP-1973-51 and the density problem GP-1973-52.

title: The loop-space target for positive and negative particles
statement: Identify the homotopy type of finite signed configurations in \(\mathbb R^n\) in which opposite particles cancel, and decide whether the target is \(\Omega^nS^n\).
status: As of November 2026, resolved by the McDuff model \(\Omega^n((S^n\times S^n)/\Delta S^n)\); the sphere-only target is incorrect for the stated cancellation topology. The 1974 page already replaces it by an unspecified2n-dimensional target; the publication is 1975. See \citet{mcduff1975configuration} and \citet[Example 11.5]{kallel1998particles}.

title: Computing local Milnor numbers from Newton data
statement: For a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point and a fixed convenient Newton boundary, find a lower bound for the Milnor number in terms of that boundary, and state coefficient conditions under which the bound is attained.
status: As of November 2026, resolved by the Newton-number inequality and equality for face-nondegenerate germs. This does not say that the Newton boundary alone determines the Milnor number of every degenerate germ. \citet[TheoremI]{kushnirenko1975newton}, received 30 September 1974 and published 1975; full treatment in \citet{kouchnirenko1976polyedres}.

title: Counting all isolated critical points from the Newton polytope
statement: For a convenient complex polynomial, bound the sum of Milnor numbers of its isolated critical points by the convex hull of 0 and its support, and characterize a generic class attaining the bound.
status: As of November 2026, resolved by the global Newton-number theorem: the count is at most the alternating coordinate-volume number and equals it under nondegeneracy at infinity. See \citet[TheoremII]{kushnirenko1975newton}. The general mixed-volume root-counting theorem is related but is not substituted for this gradient-specific assertion.

title: A measure-invariant irreducible representation of the PSL2 current group
statement: For \(C([0,1],PSL_2(\mathbb R))\) in the uniform topology, construct a nontrivial irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation whose equivalence class is unchanged by pullback along measure-preserving transformations acting on the current group, for a fixed positive Lebesgue measure. Require full interval support: currents supported in every nonempty open subinterval act nontrivially, so a finite evaluation representation is excluded.
status: As of November 2026, solved in this precise scope by the 1973 multiplicative integral of complementary-series representations; see \citet[Theorems2.2, 3.3--3.4]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions}. The earlier titles 1969-180.2/GP-1969-02 and 1969-180.1/GP-1969-01 concern related existence and classification questions, but their full formulations are unavailable here, so they are not merged or declared solved.

title: Random fields with prescribed conditional distributions
statement: For a proper consistent specification \((\gamma_V)_{V\Subset T}\) on a finite-alphabet configuration space \(X^T\), determine all probability measures satisfying \(\mu\gamma_V=\mu\) for every finite \(V\), with particular attention to existence and uniqueness.
status: As of November 2026: existence for quasilocal finite-alphabet specifications and uniqueness under Dobrushin contraction are established, as are model-dependent examples of phase coexistence. This is an expository recurrence of \citet[Section 1 and Theorems 1--2]{dobrushin1968conditional}, not a blanket claim that all specifications have been classified.
